# gzip-encoding twins — committed byte-exact

These three files exist to prove one thing that the Mall size gate depends on:

> **The same VRML text can be a legal gzip `.wrl` at wildly different sizes.**

| file | bytes | role |
|---|---:|---|
| `twin.plain.wrl` | 81,753 | the decompressed text both archives contain |
| `twin-small.wrl.gz` | 451 | DEFLATE level 9 — **at or under** the 81,290 B Mall limit |
| `twin-large.wrl.gz` | 81,781 | DEFLATE level 0 (stored) — **over** the limit |

Both archives decompress byte-for-byte to `twin.plain.wrl`, so `textBytes` and
`predictedRepackBytes` are identical for the pair. Only the *measured artifact*
differs — which is exactly why a predicted repack size can never stand in for
the size of the file that will actually be uploaded.

The pair deliberately straddles `MALL_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (81,290 B): the small
archive must PASS and the large archive must FAIL from the same text.

## Provenance and byte contract

Generated once with Node `zlib.gzipSync` at levels 9 and 0, with the gzip OS
byte forced to `0x03` and the mtime field left at 0 so the bytes are stable.
**They are committed as exact bytes and must never be regenerated by a test** —
a test that rebuilds its own oracle proves nothing. `test/fixtures/** -text` in
the root `.gitattributes` keeps Git for Windows from rewriting them, and
`test/preview/fixture-byte-contract.test.js` pins their SHA-256 digests.
